finding.claim: RejectWhenRequestBodyNotSpecified is bypassed by chunked request bodies because the check tests ContentLength > 0 and chunked requests have ContentLength -1 (PLAUSIBLE, low).
finding.source: Attacker sends a body with Transfer-Encoding: chunked; the Go server sets Request.ContentLength to -1. Precondition: the operation declares no requestBody, has no effective security requirement, and the application enabled RejectWhenRequestBodyNotSpecified.
finding.sink: validate_request.go:105 guard that should reject a body the spec does not define; the body reaches the handler.

trace.note: operation.Security nil, falls back to global security
empty security requirements return nil before any body read
requestBody nil, so ValidateRequestBody is skipped and the body is never read
ContentLength > 0 is false for -1, so no error is returned

finding.guards_checked: Option is opt-in. Security path does not read the body when no requirements exist. Non-chunked bodies with Content-Length > 0 are rejected correctly. Impact depends on whether the handler reads the body.

finding.claim: Only the first occurrence of a repeated single-valued query parameter or multipart field is validated; later values are silently ignored (PLAUSIBLE, low to medium; multipart counterpart at line 1641).
finding.source: Attacker repeats a parameter, e.g. ?role=user&role=admin, or sends two multipart parts with the same name, where the schema property is not an array.
finding.sink: Handler's use of the field. Validation checks values[0] (or first non-empty query value) and never checks the remaining occurrences.

trace.note: raw := values[0], first non-empty value used for validation
multipart: all parts appended to values[name]
obj[name] = vv[0] for non-array props; other occurrences never validated

finding.guards_checked: No option or code path rejects duplicates. The #1230 leading-empty handling does not cover this. Go stdlib Query().Get and FormValue use the first value, so stdlib handlers are consistent; exploitable only if the handler reads a different occurrence.

finding.claim: ZipFileBodyDecoder appends the full 256-byte read buffer even when Read returns fewer bytes, so stale bytes from earlier reads enter the decoded string; separately, decompression has no output cap (zip bomb DoS). Stale-buffer defect confirmed by reading; DoS documented by the function's own comment. Low, and only when the decoder is registered by the application.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied zip request body. The decoder is not registered in init() (req_resp_decoder.go:1377-1392); the application must register it.
finding.sink: The string passed to schema validation (validated value differs from archive contents) and process memory during decompression.

trace.note: rc.Read(buffer) returns n bytes, often fewer than 256 at the end of an entry
content = append(content, buffer...) appends all 256 bytes including stale data
no cap on total decompressed output across entries

finding.guards_checked: zip.NewReader uses the real body size. No output size limit exists. Stale bytes originate from the attacker's own archive, so the main effect is a validation mismatch and memory exhaustion rather than data disclosure.

finding.claim: The full request body is read into memory before the AuthenticationFunc runs, so unauthenticated clients can force unbounded buffering on operations that have a security requirement (PLAUSIBLE, low to medium; pre-authentication resource consumption, not an auth bypass).
finding.source: Unauthenticated client sends a very large request body to an operation with a security requirement.
finding.sink: Process memory. io.ReadAll buffers the whole body before AuthenticationFunc is invoked; the body is buffered again later during body validation.

trace.note: ValidateRequest calls ValidateSecurityRequirements before parameter and body validation
body replaced with an in-memory copy
AuthenticationFunc invoked only after the full read

finding.guards_checked: No size limit in this package. A limit must come from the server (for example http.MaxBytesReader), which this package does not require.
